title: A blended genome and exome sequencing method captures genetic variation in an unbiased and cost-effective manner.
data_url: dbGaP phs001642.v1.p1 and phs002502.v3.p1 (controlled access); NeuroGAP via NIMH Data Archive (NDA, controlled) or by email

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the data availability statement in the PMC BioC full text: the individual-level data (one CRAM per person plus quality-controlled VCFs) sit in dbGaP studies phs001642 and phs002502 and the NIMH Data Archive, all of which need an access application. Opened the only open deposit, Zenodo record 18791381: a single 1.2 MB zip of the atgu/bge_analysis code (CC-BY-4.0), with no data in it. The Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint returned no zip.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 53,446 PUMAS samples (from the GPC, Paisa and NeuroGAP-Psychosis cohorts), imputation R² of at least 0.90 against Global Screening Array genotypes, about 90% PPV (positive predictive value) for copy-number variants spanning 3 or more exons, and the 400-person SSC benchmark set. None of this was checked in files.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked the data availability statement: the data are in dbGaP (phs001642, phs002502) and NDA (NIMH Data Archive). Both are controlled access and need an application. The open Zenodo deposit holds code only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked because A1 failed. Any label, such as whether a call is correct against deep WGS (whole-genome sequencing), would have to be built by comparing BGE calls with gold-standard calls from matched samples.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked. The inputs are CRAM alignment files and VCFs behind controlled access.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not checked. The paper reports 53,446 samples, but the files are inaccessible.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Per-person CRAM files for about 53,000 people: likely terabytes (estimate; not seen).
a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw alignments at genome scale do not fit on a laptop.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked. Imputed genotypes are themselves the output of a model (GLIMPSE2).

plain_idea.one_liner: Use features of cheap low-depth genome reads to predict which imputed or copy-number calls agree with expensive deep sequencing.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-variant or per-call features from blended genome-exome data for people who also have deep genome or genotyping-array data. Number of examples unknown, because the data are controlled access.
plain_idea.predict: Whether each call matches the gold standard: deep 30x whole-genome calls (400 people from the Simons Simplex Collection) or Illumina array genotypes.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups sequencing underrepresented populations at low cost could flag unreliable calls. But the data need a dbGaP or NDA application, so the project cannot start.

ml_idea: Learn a calibrated quality score for BGE (blended genome-exome) imputed variants or copy-number calls, using deep WGS (whole-genome sequencing) or array genotypes as truth. Blocked by controlled access.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the data are inaccessible without a dbGaP or NDA application.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement. Done: it lists dbGaP and NDA controlled access only.

verdict_reason: A1 fails. All individual-level data (CRAM and VCF files) are in dbGaP (phs001642, phs002502) and the NIMH Data Archive, which need an access application, and the only open deposit, on Zenodo, is code. The data are also raw genome-scale alignments, far beyond a laptop.
